models.author: Radim Közl
models.description:
# Model Summary

This model is a **Neuro-symbolic Vision Transformer**. It combines a ViT-Tiny backbone for feature extraction with a [JAX Logical Neural Network (JLNN)](https://github.com/RadimKozl/JLNN) for interpretable reasoning. Unlike standard models, it outputs not just a class, but a logical justification and an uncertainty interval [L, U].

### JLNN documentation

- [Tutorial: JLNN + Vision Transformer: Neuro-symbolic Image Classification](https://radimkozl.github.io/JLNN/tutorials/JLNN_vit_training.html)
- [GitHub: Colab notebook](https://github.com/RadimKozl/JLNN/blob/main/examples/JLNN_vit_training_github.ipynb)

## Usage

The model outputs a tuple containing three distinct levels of information. This is essential for the neuro-symbolic audit trail.

### Inference Example (Python/JAX):

```python
# input_img shape: (batch, 224, 224, 3)
results = model(input_img)

audit_logic = results[0]  # [L, U] intervals for logical rules
grounding   = results[1]  # Fuzzy truth for basic predicates (head, body, etc.)
logits      = results[2]  # Standard classification logits

# Get predicted class
predicted_class = jnp.argmax(logits, axis=-1)

# Check why it was classified (Audit Rule 0)
print(f"Rule 0 Truth (Lower, Upper): {audit_logic[0, 0]}")
```

**Technical Specs**

- **Input:** `float32[batch, 224, 224, 3]` (Normalized to 0-1)
- **Audit Logic:** `float32[batch, 47, 2]` (For 47 rules in this setup)
- **Grounding:** `float32[batch, n_predicates, 2]`
- **Logits:** `float32[batch, 10]` (For CIFAR-10)

## System

This is a standalone model but designed to be part of an **explainable AI (XAI)** pipeline. Downstream applications can use the logical "Audit" trail to verify why the model made a specific decision (e.g., "identified as animal because head and eyes were detected").

## Implementation requirements

- **Hardware:** Trained on Google Colab (TPU v5e-1).
- **Software:** JAX/Flax NNX, JLNN (JAX Logical Neural Networks), Optax, Orbax (checkpointing), Grain (data loading), OpenCV (image processing), Xarray (logic monitoring)
- **Inference:** Native **StableHLO** export. This allows the model to be compiled and executed efficiently across various hardware backends (CPU, GPU, TPU) using the JAX ecosystem or a dedicated StableHLO interpreter.

# Model Characteristics

## Model initialization

The entire architecture, including the **Vision Transformer (ViT) backbone**, **Fuzzy Grounding**, and **JLNN layers**, is **initialized and trained from scratch**. No pre-trained weights were used. This demonstrates the model's ability to learn complex visual features and their logical relationships simultaneously from the provided dataset.

## Model stats

- **Size:** Approx. 20-25 MB
- **Architecture:** ViT-Tiny (Patch size 16, 12 layers, 192 embedding dim) + Linear Grounding + JLNN.
- **Params:** ~5.7M parameters.
- **Latency:** Low latency inference on CPU/TPU thanks to the StableHLO compilation.

## Other details

- **Quantization:** None (FP32).
- **Privacy:** No differential privacy techniques applied.

## Training data

**[CIFAR-10](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/blourdhuraju/cifar-10)** dataset. Images were upscaled to 224x224 and normalizet with ImageNet normalization.

## Demographic groups

Not applicable (General object recognition).

## Evaluation data

- **Split:** 45,000 training images / 10,000 test images.
- **Difference:** Test data consists of the standard [CIFAR-10](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/blourdhuraju/cifar-10) test set.

# Evaluation Results

## Summary

The model achieves competitive accuracy on [CIFAR-10](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/blourdhuraju/cifar-10) while providing 100% transparency in the reasoning process.

## Fairness 

Fairness is defined as **Logical Consistency**. The model is penalized if its visual detections (grounding) contradict the defined logical rules.

## Usage limitations

- Performance is limited by the quality of the defined logical rules.
- Designed for datasets where semantic parts (like "head", "eyes") can be mapped to visual features.

## Ethics

The developers focused on **Transparency**. By using [JLNN](https://github.com/RadimKozl/JLNN), we mitigate the "black-box" risk of deep learning, allowing humans to audit and correct the model's logic if biased or incorrect rules are learned.

models.description:
# Model Summary:VT-FineTuned

This model is a domain-specific vision encoder optimized for the **DeepFashion In-Shop Clothes Retrieval** task. It is based on the CLIP (ViT-B-16) architecture and has been fine-tuned using supervised contrastive learning to align consumer and shop-shot garment views in a unified latent space.

## Usage

### Implementation Snippet
The model is designed to be loaded via PyTorch and used within the `FashionEmbeddingModel` class.
```python
import torch
import open_clip
from PIL import Image

# 1. Load Model (CLIP ViT-B-16)
model, _, preprocess = open_clip.create_model_and_transforms('ViT-B-16', pretrained='openai')
# Load Fine-Tuned Weights
state_dict = torch.load("clip_finetuned.pt", map_location="cpu")
model.visual.load_state_dict(state_dict)

# 2. Prepare Input
image = preprocess(Image.open("query.jpg")).unsqueeze(0) # Shape: [1, 3, 224, 224]

# 3. Generate Embedding
with torch.no_grad():
    embedding = model.encode_image(image) # Shape: [1, 512]
    embedding /= embedding.norm(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
```

### Constraints & Failures
- **Input Requirements**: Requires 224x224 RGB images.
- **Failure Cases**: Performance degrades on heavily occluded items or images where the garment takes up less than 15% of the frame (mitigated by the YOLO/SegFormer preprocessing stages).

## System
This model is the core **Embedder** in a multi-stage visual search system:
1.  **Detector (YOLOv8)**: Extracts garment bounding boxes.
2.  **Segmenter (SegFormer)**: Generates pixel-accurate masks.
3.  **Embedder (This Model)**: Projects masked garments into a 512-D vector space.
4.  **Indexer (HNSW)**: Performs Approximate Nearest Neighbor search.

## Implementation Requirements
- **Training Hardware**: NVIDIA Tesla T4 GPU (Kaggle Environment).
- **Inference Hardware**: Real-time performance achieved on consumer-grade GPUs (e.g., RTX 3060) or T4 instances.
- **Compute Metrics**: 
    - Training Time: ~4 hours for 3 epochs on the full In-Shop dataset.
    - Inference Latency: ~28ms per image (embedding stage only).

---

# Model Characteristics

## Model Initialization
The model was not trained from scratch. It utilizes **Pre-trained Weights from OpenAI (CLIP ViT-B-16)** and was fine-tuned specifically on fashion pairs.

## Model Stats
- **Size**: ~600 MB (float32 weights).
- **Architecture**: 12-layer Vision Transformer (ViT).
- **Embedding Dimension**: 512.
- **Total Parameters**: ~86M.

## Other Details
The model is optimized for precision. No quantization or pruning has been applied in the current version to preserve maximum retrieval fidelity (NDCG).

---

# Data Overview

## Training Data
- **Source**: [DeepFashion In-Shop Clothes Retrieval](https://mmlab.ie.cuhk.edu.hk/projects/DeepFashion/InShopRetrieval.html).
- **Composition**: 52,712 images of 7,982 items. 
- **Processing**: We used a "Consumer-to-Shop" strategy, pairing different views of the same `item_id` for contrastive alignment.

## Evaluation Data
- **Splits**: Standard DeepFashion partition (Train/Query/Gallery).
- **Query Set**: ~3,500 distinct items.
- **Gallery Set**: ~12,600 product images.

---

# Evaluation Results

## Summary
The model demonstrates a significant breakthrough in retrieval accuracy, outperforming the zero-shot baseline by a substantial margin.
- **Detailed Metrics**: See the [Ablation Study Results](RESULTS.md).
- **Best Performance (Condition C)**: **85.7% Recall@10**.

## Usage Limitations
- **Generalization**: While excellent for fashion, the model is not intended for generic object retrieval (e.g., cars, animals).
- **Bias**: The dataset primarily contains high-quality studio shots and user-generated content from specific fashion platforms, which may limit performance on very low-lighting or grainy mobile captures.

## Ethics & Fairness
- **Risk Mitigation**: The use of SegFormer masking helps ensure the model focuses on the garment rather than the person, reducing potential demographic bias related to skin tone or body shape.
- **Intended Use**: This model is built for information retrieval and e-commerce assistance. It is not designed for person identification or surveillance.

instances.overview:
**Identifier**: `fashionret-clip-vit-b16-ft-viva-v1`  
**Checkpoint**: `clip_finetuned.pt`  
**Optimization Target**: High-recall in-shop garment retrieval.

#### Technical Metadata:
- **Framework**: PyTorch 2.1+ / `open-clip-torch`
- **Backbone**: ViT-B-16 (Vision Transformer)
- **Latent Dimension**: 512 (L2-Normalized)
- **Input Tensor**: (3, 224, 224) RGB

This specific model instance is a domain-specialized vision encoder derived from the **OpenAI CLIP (ViT-B-16)** foundation. It has been fine-tuned using a **supervised contrastive learning** objective on the DeepFashion dataset. The primary architectural innovation in this instance is the strategic unfreezing of the final transformer blocks, allowing the model to transition from generic visual primitives to fashion-specific semantic manifolds. It serves as the "Gold Standard" weights for the Condition C ablation study, delivering the project's peak retrieval performance.

models.provenanceSources:
### Data Procurement
The underlying training data was procured from the **MMLAB (The Chinese University of Hong Kong)**. 
- **Source**: DeepFashion In-Shop Clothes Retrieval Benchmark.
- **Acquisition**: Data was obtained via an academic request process and processed locally into a contrastive pair format.
- **Filtering**: We strictly utilized the `item_id` associations to create "Consumer-to-Shop" and "Cross-View" positive pairs, while negative pairs were sampled within the same batch during training.

### Model Procurement (Weight Generation)
The final model weights (`clip_finetuned.pt`) were procured through an iterative training process:
1.  **Base Selection**: Initialized from the `openai/clip-vit-b-16` pre-trained checkpoint.
2.  **Environment**: Provisioned a high-compute instance on **Kaggle** (NVIDIA Tesla T4).
3.  **Refinement**: Executed a 3-epoch contrastive fine-tuning loop with a specialized AdamW optimizer.
4.  **Verification**: Procurement was finalized only after the weights demonstrated a **>30% Recall@10 improvement** over the baseline in the ablation suite.

This repository contains fine-tuned Transformer-based models for detecting online gambling promotion spam ("judol") in Indonesian YouTube comments. Four pre-trained multilingual and Indonesian-specific BERT models were fine-tuned on a labeled dataset of Indonesian YouTube comments and are available in two variations: default (initial training) and retrained-models (further trained on an expanded dataset via semi-supervised pseudo-labeling).
Models available: IndoBERT · IndoBERTweet · XLM-RoBERTa · mBERT
Task: Binary Text Classification (Normal / Judol)
Language: Indonesian (Bahasa Indonesia)
Best performance (IndoBERT retrained): up to 99.60% F1-Macro and 0.994 ROC-AUC

instances.overview: Initial fine-tuned models trained on the first labeled dataset consisting of manually annotated Indonesian YouTube comments. These models serve as the base annotation models used in the semi-supervised labeling pipeline.

Retrained versions of the initial models, further fine-tuned on an expanded dataset of ~20,000 additional comments that were auto-labeled via 4-model ensemble voting. These models generally achieve improved performance over the default variation and are recommended for inference.

# viki-neural-forge

**Local LLM · Ollama · VIKI Neural Forge · self-hosted AI · private assistant**

**viki-neural-forge** is an **Ollama** model image produced by **[VIKI](https://github.com/Orythix/VIKI-public)** (**Virtual Intelligence Knowledge Interface**) **Neural Forge**: your **base** checkpoint (e.g. **Qwen**, **Gemma**, **Llama-class**, **Mistral**, **DeepSeek**, **Phi**) plus a baked **`Modelfile` `SYSTEM`** block—**persona**, **reinforced lessons**, and **generation parameters**. It is **not** a separate foundation model; **reasoning traces**, **tool calling**, **vision**, **audio**, and **context length** follow the **base** you set in `FROM`.

Use it for **offline LLM** chat, **RAG-style** behavior hints in the prompt, and a consistent **VIKI** voice when paired with the full **Python** agent (optional). **Documentation:** [Orythix/VIKI-public](https://github.com/Orythix/VIKI-public).

## Pull and run

```bash
ollama pull orythix/viki-neural-forge
ollama run orythix/viki-neural-forge
```

```bash
ollama show orythix/viki-neural-forge --modelfile
```

## VIKI agent platform (what the project offers)

Running the **full VIKI application** (not this file alone) unlocks an **autonomous AI agent**, **sovereign AI** / **privacy-first** stack: **local-first**, **air-gapped** mode, **Orythix** cognitive architecture, **judgment engine** (reflex / shallow / deep), **capability gating**, **ethical governor**, **reflection** layer, **SQLite** lessons and **semantic memory**, **failure memory**, **continuous learning**, **Neural Forge** (`viki-neural-forge` / **`viki-evolved`** profile), **multi-model routing**, **ensemble** deliberation (optional), **low-resource mode**, **prewarm** for Ollama.

**Interfaces:** **CLI**, **Flask REST API**, **SSE** chat streaming, **WebSocket** missions, **React** + **Vite** **dashboard**, **hologram** voice UI, **lite** UI mode.

**Tools & skills (representative):** **MCP** integration; **RAG** / retrieval; **filesystem**, **shell**, **sandboxed** Python; **browser** automation (**Playwright**); **research** / web; **vision**; **Whisper** / **STT**; **TTS**; **PDF**; **data analysis** (CSV/Excel, charts); **presentations** (PPTX); **spreadsheets** (XLSX); **website** scaffold; **computer-use** / grounding (e.g. OmniParser ONNX); **code** workflows; **engineering playbooks**; **LSP** bridge (**pyright**, **TypeScript** language server).

**Integrations:** **Telegram**, **Discord**, **Slack**, **WhatsApp**; **email**, **calendar**; **Obsidian**; **smart home** (e.g. Hue); **Twitter**; **Things 3** / file tasks; optional **cloud** LLM profiles when not **local LLM only**.

**Operator & missions:** **mission** graph, **sub-agents**, **traces**, **best-of-N** worktrees, **forge** promote/rollback API, **slash** commands (`/restore`, `/undo`), **subtasks** / **total_steps** progress.

**Security & ops:** **API key** auth, **admin** secret, **safety** envelope, **endpoint guard**, optional **security scan**, **Docker**, **sandbox**, structured **logging**, **SECURITY** / **SECURITY_SETUP** docs.

*This Ollama artifact is the **baked model** slice; **MCP**, **browser**, **RAG DB**, and **missions** require the **VIKI** runtime.*

## Good use cases (this Ollama image)

- **Self-hosted** chat and **offline** assistant behavior (with a capable **base**)
- **Private** instruction tuning via **system prompt** (no extra **pretraining**)
- **Q&A**, **summarization**, **coding** help, **documents**, **multimodal** Q&A—when the **base** supports them
- Same **VIKI** “voice” as in-app when you point **`viki-evolved`** / **`model_name`** at **`viki-neural-forge`**

## Build your own Neural Forge image

With the VIKI implementation checkout:

```bash
python scripts/build_viki_model.py
```

Public index: [Documentation](https://github.com/Orythix/VIKI-public/blob/main/docs/DOCUMENTATION.md) · Main README section: *Build your VIKI model* (in full repo docs).

## License and commercial use

**Commercial use** follows the **license of the underlying base weights**. The Forge layer adds **text** and **parameters** only. **VIKI** tooling is **Apache 2.0**; you must comply with the **base model** vendor.
